title: The road just outside Coventry named among UK's most haunted
excerpt: The A46 between Leamington and Coventry features on a list of the UK's most haunted roads, with tales of faint bell chimes near Gaveston's Cross and an athlete's mysterious disappearance.
content:
A stretch of the A46 between Leamington and Coventry has been named among the UK's most haunted roads, with eerie legends linked to woodland just off the route.

Global car rental comparison site DiscoverCars.com included the Warwickshire road in its round-up of allegedly haunted routes across the UK and Europe ahead of Halloween.

At the heart of the local ghost stories is Gaveston's Cross, which stands in private woodland near the A46. According to legend, Piers Gaveston was beheaded at the spot in 1312.

A sandstone cross marks the site, where it is claimed faint bell chimes can be heard on a still night.

Another tale associated with the area concerns James Burne Worson, an athlete who supposedly vanished into thin air and was never found. However, this story was fiction, written by author Ambrose Bierce, rather than an account of a real disappearance.

Bierce himself went missing years later, after writing a cryptic letter to a friend. It read: "As to me, I leave here tomorrow for an unknown destination."

The A46 is one of six UK roads on DiscoverCars.com's list. Others include Berkeley Square in London, linked to a ghostly white apparition, and the B1249 in East Riding, Yorkshire, where a werewolf-like creature is said to prowl.

Also featured are Hangman's Hill beside Epping Forest in Essex, the junction of Cambridge Gardens and St Mark's Road in London's Ladbroke Grove, associated with a phantom bus, and the A12 between Great Yarmouth and Lowestoft.

Aleksandrs Buraks, head of growth at DiscoverCars.com, said: "As Halloween approaches, now is a great time to learn about the allegedly haunted roads near you, along with the haunting backstories behind them all. We found that there's a huge amount of ghost stories and urban legends all across the UK, which make up much of our list."

He also urged motorists to drive carefully at night and pay particular attention on unfamiliar roads.

Other haunted roads

Berkeley Square, London, England

Berkeley Square may look like any other road in London, but it has an eerie past and was one of “the most feared places in Britain". 50 Berkeley Square in particular was believed to be where the hauntings stem from. Legend has it a ghostly white apparition haunts this area, believed to be that of a woman who jumped from the window of the property.

B1249, East Riding, Yorkshire, England

On this road in Yorkshire, it’s believed that a nightmarish werewolf creature lurks in the area. The most prominent account of this creature was documented in the 1960s by Charles Christian, who wrote about the moment he found a lorry driver who had his vehicle destroyed by a “red-eyed hairy creature” who smashed his windscreen. Further sightings have also been reported, notably in 2016 by a terrified driver who reported seeing a bigfoot-like creature.

Hangman’s Hill, Essex, UK

Next to Epping Forest in Essex is Hangman’s Hill, a road with a haunting reputation. It’s been said that cars parked in neutral at the foot of the hill have been pulled up towards the hill towards an ancient tree where it’s believed people have lost their lives there. Locals describe an “odd feeling to the place”, with sensations of feeling watched and unexplainable flashes of light.

Intersection of Cambridge Gardens and St Mark’s Road, Ladbroke Grove, London, England

This section of Ladbroke Grove was allegedly once haunted by a phantom bus, which may have led to a fatal accident. In 1934 at 1:15 AM, eyewitnesses report seeing a car driving down the empty road, when suddenly a red double-decker bus appeared. The driver of the car swerved into a building where the car caught fire. The bus vanished into thin air, and in years to come, many other sightings of this bus were reported until the road was redesigned in the 1990s.

A12, Great Yarmouth to Lowestoft, England

This road is allegedly haunted by a ghost known as the sneering man of Croton. Drivers have reported seeing an unnerving sneering face when passing by. It’s believed that three people lost their life on this road, including a lorry driver whose vehicle careened off the road and into the trees for no particular reason. One survivor from an accident on the road reports seeing a spectral elderly man.
